newsitem.title: CANADA: Petro-Canada reports sharply lower profits.
newsitem.headline: Petro-Canada reports sharply lower profits.

text.p: Petro-Canada Thursday reported sharply lower third-quarter earnings, the latest in a string of weak quarterly data from Canada's integrated oil sector.
While crude oil prices have risen sharply, Petro-Canada was unable to enjoy some of the big price rises because it had hedged half of its crude oil production at lower price levels.

Blaming high crude oil prices and gasoline price wars, the company said third-quarter net earnings fell to C$24 million ($18 million), or C8 cents (6 cents), a share from C$79 million ($58 million), or C32 cents (24 cents) a share, last year.
Revenues climbed to C$359 million ($266 million) from C$308 million ($228 million) in 1995.
Petro-Canada's weaker showing followed poor third-quarter results from other Canadian integrated oil companies Suncor Inc., Shell Canada Ltd. and Imperial Oil Ltd..
Those firms also cited shrinking oil refinery profit margins, as crude oil prices reached a six-year high, and brutal gasoline price wars in Quebec for their weak showings.

Petro-Canada also late last year hedged, or sold forward contracts at a fixed price, half of its 1996 crude oil production at $18.04 a barrel, forcing it to sit on the sidelines as many other oil companies reaped the benefit of big price gains.

Petro-Canada said the hedging activities in its exploration and production division translated into C$32 million ($24 million) in foregone earnings during the first nine months of the year. The company said it would review its management strategy for oil price hedging.
